# SEO-084: Apply a noindex directive only where exclusion from the index is intended

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `robots` |
| Category | `TECHNICAL_SEO` |
| Minimum level | `LITE` |

| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

Every page carrying a robots noindex directive is on a list of pages the site has decided should not be indexed, and no page outside that list carries one.

## Rationale

A noindex directive removes a page from search entirely, and because nothing about the rendered page looks different, one left behind by a template default or a staging build can stay unnoticed indefinitely.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Write the intended exclusion list down as data and derive the directive from it, rather than setting it per template. Never add or remove the directive on a page without first confirming which side of that list the page belongs on.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Collect the robots directives from both the meta element and the response header of every sampled route and compare the resulting set against the intended exclusion list.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `HTTP_HEADER`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: `robots-meta-noindex-unintended`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
